messages.author: 71bfb5f1e96782a8
messages.subject: combine table and figure
parts:
Dear list,

i would like to build a graph like this in ggplot:
http://www.cmaj.ca/content/183/13/1474/F2.medium.gif

i tried to store all the information in the axis label:

x=data.frame(name=c("Disease1 \t OR=9.5 \t CI=(9,10)",
"Disease2withalongername \t OR=9.5 \t CI=(9,10)"),value=1:2)
ggplot(data=x, aes(x=value, y=name))+geom_point()

and it looks already quite good, but i would like to have coloumn
heads (OR, CI), for example. Is it possible to put a complete table as
axis-values?

Best,
Felix

messages.author: affa918ed63b6275
messages.subject: Re: combine table and figure
parts:
Hi,

Unfortunately no. You need a deep hack to do that.
But I feel the idea is quite interesting.
Maybe it will be implemented in future, along with development of axis guides.

Also, this type of axis seems to be popular, at least in physiology and biology.
http://www.pnas.org/content/101/8/2590/F1.expansion.html
I don't know the name of this kind of axis for relative value. Do anyone know?

In my view, the "axis" is something that the coordinate is defined against plot.
In this sense, all the axes, the table axis, relative-value axis, and
position axis (current implement) share the same thing.
Anyway, the axis can be extended in more flexible way without loosing
ggplot2's strength.

--

The University of  Tokyo, Japan.

I believe this is called a forest plot, implemented in the metafor
package. The package has a vignette which corresponds to a paper
published in the Journal of Statistical Software.

Dennis
